live.instructions: Free expense reporting in chat: receipts, mileage at the real IRS rate, and clean PDF/XLSX reports with live status links. Call get_capabilities to explain the product (works signed out). Every other tool requires sign-in via this connector's OAuth flow — signing in keeps the user's ledger and unlocks mileage memory.

tools.name: get_capabilities
tools.title: What PuraFi Can Do
tools.description: Explains what the PuraFi Expense Agent can do. Call when the user asks what this connector is, what it can do, or how to get started. Works without sign-in.

tools.name: my_account
tools.title: My Account
tools.description: Returns who this user is and how they file expenses: emails, ledger counts, AND their saved setup — default approver, employee ID / department / cost center, and whether their company requires a receipt for every expense. CALL THIS EARLY in any expense session so you use what they've already told us instead of asking again; `setup_missing` lists what's still worth asking once. Requires a linked account.

tools.name: add_receipt
tools.title: Add Receipt
tools.description: Saves a NEW receipt to the user's expense ledger. Call ONCE per new expense the user shares (photo, PDF, screenshot, pasted text, or description) — never to display the ledger (that's my_receipts) and never to correct an existing entry (that's update_expense). An exact duplicate (same merchant, date, amount) is refused unless allow_duplicate is set; if the duplicate call carries an image and the existing entry has none, the image is attached to the existing entry instead. If this host cannot pass file attachments as tool parameters, read the receipt image yourself and pass the extracted fields — omit receipt_image entirely. Requires a linked account.

date.description: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD, the expense date

category.description: Free text; normalized to the PuraFi category enum

business_purpose.description: Required before export — what this expense was for. For meals, travel, and lodging include WHERE (city or venue), e.g. 'Client dinner re Q3 partnership — Austin, TX'; ask the user if unknown

attendees.description: Required for meals: who attended, WITH business relationship, e.g. 'Dan Hughes (PuraFi, CEO)' — the IRS substantiation standard, not just names

allow_duplicate.description: Set ONLY after the user confirms this really is a second, separate purchase with identical merchant, date, and amount

trip.description: Trip label if part of a trip, e.g. 'Austin onsite'

receipt_image.description: The user's uploaded receipt photo/PDF — pass the file the user attached

receipt_image_url.description: Fallback: a public https URL of the receipt image if no file upload

expense_url.description: Deep link to this expense's edit page on the web dashboard

tools.name: my_receipts
tools.title: My Receipts
tools.description: Lists the user's unsubmitted ledger (receipts + mileage), grouped by trip or month, with totals. Call when the user asks what's in their ledger or wants a summary. Requires a linked account.

category.description: Canonical category enum — drives the row icon

href.description: Web dashboard page for this row — the widget opens it externally

dashboard_url.description: Web dashboard for editing and managing the ledger

tools.name: log_mileage
tools.title: Log Mileage
tools.description: Logs a mileage expense from a described drive. Distance is computed server-side (mapping API) at the IRS rate for the drive date — do NOT estimate distance or quote a rate yourself. If the user states the distance explicitly, pass it as `miles`. Requires a linked account.

from.description: Start location as the user described it

to.description: Destination as the user described it

date.description: Drive date ISO YYYY-MM-DD; defaults to today

trip.description: Trip label if part of a trip, e.g. 'Austin onsite'

miles.description: One-way miles, ONLY if the user stated the distance

expense_url.description: Deep link to this expense's edit page on the web dashboard

tools.name: update_expense
tools.title: Update Expense
tools.description: Updates an expense already in the user's unsubmitted ledger. Use when the user corrects or changes an expense they added (amount, date, category, purpose, attendees…) — or shares a receipt image for an expense that's already in the ledger (pass receipt_image; never re-add it). Expenses already in a report are frozen. For mileage entries only the date and purpose can change — re-log the drive to change the route. Requires a linked account.

id.description: The receipt_id or mileage_id from add_receipt/log_mileage/my_receipts

purpose.description: Mileage only: the drive's business purpose

receipt_image.description: Receipt photo/PDF to attach to this expense (replaces any current image)

receipt_image_url.description: Fallback: a public https URL of the receipt image if no file upload

expense_url.description: Deep link to this expense's edit page on the web dashboard

tools.name: delete_expense
tools.title: Delete Expense
tools.description: Permanently deletes an expense from the user's unsubmitted ledger. Use when the user asks to remove an expense they added. Expenses already in a report cannot be deleted. Requires a linked account.

id.description: The receipt_id or mileage_id to delete

tools.name: my_dashboard
tools.title: My Dashboard
tools.description: Shows the user's whole expense picture in one full-screen card: unsubmitted total, money owed to them, reports awaiting review, the full unsubmitted ledger and every report with its status. Read-only — nothing is changed. Use when the user asks for an overview, “where do I stand”, “show me everything”, “open my dashboard”, or wants to see reports and expenses together rather than one list. For just the ledger use my_receipts; for one report's status use my_reimbursement_status. Requires a linked account.

category.description: Canonical category enum — drives the row icon

href.description: Web dashboard page for this row — the widget opens it externally

tools.name: recall_report
tools.title: Recall Report
tools.description: Pulls a SENT report back for editing. The approver's one-click link stops working immediately and the report becomes a draft again, still holding the same expenses — so the user fixes what was wrong and calls submit_my_report again rather than starting over. Use when they say they sent it to the wrong person, spotted a mistake, or want to add something before their manager reviews it. Only reports that are awaiting review or whose link expired can be recalled; once approved, rejected or paid a decision has been made and the report is frozen — export a corrected one instead. TELL THE USER their approver's link is now dead and that the report needs resubmitting. Requires a linked account.

report_id.description: The report_id from make_my_expense_report or my_reimbursement_status

recipient.description: Who held the now-dead approval link

report_status.description: Set when the report was too far along to recall

tools.name: delete_report
tools.title: Delete Draft Report
tools.description: Deletes a DRAFT expense report the user no longer wants. The expenses inside it are NOT destroyed — they go straight back to the unsubmitted ledger, so the user can fix something and rebuild. Also works on reports the user marked completed by hand. Reports already sent for approval (submitted/approved/paid) are frozen for audit and cannot be deleted. Use my_reimbursement_status to find the report id. Requires a linked account.

released_count.description: Expenses handed back to the unsubmitted ledger

report_status.description: Set when the report was too far along to delete

tools.name: set_my_expense_rules
tools.title: Update My Settings
tools.description: THE way to change any account setting from chat — everything the web settings page can edit. Use it whenever the user says things like “change my manager/approver to …”, “my finance contact is …”, “send my reports to … from now on”, “update my employee ID / department / cost center”, “my company requires receipts”, or anything phrased as changing their settings, profile or defaults. default_recipient is the approver (manager or finance) every future report is submitted to — it goes live immediately. employee ID, department and cost center print on every report header. Company categories and stated rules are kept as remembered notes only: do not promise they change how reports render or enforce anything — today they don't. Pass ONLY the fields being changed; the rest are preserved. my_account reads the current values back. Requires a linked account.

require_receipts.description: Company requires a receipt for EVERY expense — reports will flag any line missing one

tools.name: import_my_history
tools.title: Import History
tools.description: Seeds the ledger from existing records. Accepts CSV text with lines of: merchant, amount, date(YYYY-MM-DD)[, category][, notes]. Use when the user pastes or uploads an existing expense spreadsheet. Requires a linked account.

csv.description: CSV rows; a header line is auto-detected and skipped

tools.name: make_my_expense_report
tools.title: Make Expense Report
tools.description: Builds a clean expense report (PDF or XLSX) from the user's unsubmitted ledger and returns a download link, plus CSV, XLSX, and QuickBooks-ready CSV artifacts. Scope it with `trip` or a date range when the user asks for a specific trip/month/period — unscoped, it includes EVERYTHING unsubmitted (say so if the ledger holds unrelated items; my_receipts shows what's there). Expenses outside the scope stay in the ledger for a later report. Safe to call again after adding expenses: an existing draft in scope is absorbed into the rebuilt report (never duplicated), and calling with nothing new returns the same draft unchanged. Requires a linked account.

period.description: Label for the report header, e.g. 'July 2026' or 'Austin trip'

trip.description: Build ONLY expenses tagged with this trip label (as shown by my_receipts grouped by trip)

date_from.description: Build only expenses on/after this ISO date YYYY-MM-DD

date_to.description: Build only expenses on/before this ISO date YYYY-MM-DD

report_items.description: Line items — the widget's per-category dropdowns

category.description: Canonical category enum — drives the row icon

href.description: Web dashboard page for this row — the widget opens it externally

ledger_cleared.description: True when building moved these expenses out of the unsubmitted ledger

files_url.description: Tokenized page with every format + receipt images, no sign-in

dashboard_url.description: Web dashboard for managing expenses and reports

tools.name: submit_my_report
tools.title: Submit Report
tools.description: Submits a drafted report: registers it with the approval service (14-day magic link) and emails the approver the PDF + CSV with a one-click Review & Approve button. THIS SENDS REAL MAIL AND CANNOT BE RECALLED — pass `report_id` whenever you know which report the user means (make_my_expense_report returns it). Omitting it only works when exactly one draft exists and it was just built; otherwise the tool returns status `needs_target` with the candidate reports — show the user their titles, totals and ages, ask which one, then call again with that report_id. Re-sending an already-submitted report (typo'd address) also requires an explicit report_id, because it invalidates the link the approver already has. Requires a linked account.

recipient_email.description: Manager/finance email if not using the saved default

remember_recipient.description: Save recipient_email as the user's default approver for future reports. Set true when they say this is their (new) manager/finance contact; leave unset for a one-off send.

saved_default.description: Approver future reports will go to

default_differs.description: Sent somewhere other than the saved default, which is unchanged

candidates.description: Reports the user might have meant — ask which one, then call again with report_id

tools.name: email_my_report
tools.title: Email My Report
tools.description: Emails the report's files (PDF + CSV attached, Excel/QuickBooks linked) to the USER themselves — or any address they name, like their accountant or an AP inbox. This is the self-service path for people whose company has its own filing process: NO approval link is included and nothing changes state. Use submit_my_report instead when a manager should approve. Defaults to the latest report and the user's own email. Requires a linked account.

to.description: Destination email; omit to send to the user's own address

tools.name: mark_reimbursed
tools.title: Mark Reimbursed
tools.description: The money arrived — closes an approved (or manually-completed) report as PAID and stops its days-owed counter. Call when the user says they got reimbursed. Defaults to the most recent approved/completed report. Requires a linked account.

tools.name: my_reimbursement_status
tools.title: Reimbursement Status
tools.description: Shows every report's status (draft / submitted / approved / rejected / expired / paid) with a days-waiting counter for anything pending. Call when the user asks where their money is. When they say the money arrived, follow with mark_reimbursed. Requires a linked account.

owed_total.description: Sum of submitted + approved (not yet paid) report totals — the answer to 'how much am I owed'

dashboard_url.description: Web dashboard for managing expenses and reports
